haiku-low.q1: In step 5, after the lint passes and before any new instance starts, on the shared PostgreSQL database. The live release must keep working, since migrations are additive only.
haiku-low.q2: Only in a later release, after the release that uses the old column or table has been retired.
haiku-low.q3: All 4 new instances must be healthy and pass smoke tests within 10 minutes of step 6. If not, step 9 aborts and the public listener is untouched.
haiku-low.q4: One change repoints the public listener from the old target group to the new one, with no gradual shift. Then tags are set: new live, old rollback-window.
haiku-low.q5: A 5xx rate above 1% over any 5-minute window within 15 minutes after the switch. Rollback repoints the listener, tags old live and new failed, and shuts down the new instances. Migrations are left alone.
haiku-low.q6: Until 30 minutes after the switch time. After that the old colour is shut down, so a manual rollback is refused; fixes then go out as a normal deploy of the previous release.
haiku-low.q7: Migrations that already finished stay applied and are not reversed. The failed one is not applied, and an invalid index may remain. The deploy stops, the live colour keeps serving, and a re-run follows the fix.
haiku-low.q8: The live colour is the target group the public listener forwards to; the other is idle and gets the release. Only the listener records live; state tags sit on target groups.
haiku-low.q9: CI's single-run deploy lock on catalog-web blocks overlapping deploys. It is held until step 15, which can be up to 30 minutes after the switch.
haiku-low.q10: A second load balancer listener, reachable only from CI, whose rule step 6 repoints to the idle target group, so smoke tests reach the new instances.
haiku-low.q11: The migration tool, run once in step 5. Its history table records applied migrations, and IF NOT EXISTS makes any re-run safe.
haiku-low.q12: After an abort or rollback, the new instances are shut down, leaving the idle colour empty. If shutdown fails, step 2 of the next deploy shuts them down.

sonnet.q1: Step 5, after the lint passes and before any new-release instance starts. The live (old) release must still work against the migrated database, because migrations are additive only.
sonnet.q2: Only in a later release, after the release that used the old column or table has been retired. The lint rejects drops and renames in the same release.
sonnet.q3: All 4 new instances must be healthy (/healthz) and the smoke tests must pass through the test listener, all within 10 minutes of step 6. If not, the deploy aborts (step 9): the new instances are shut down, the public listener and live colour are untouched, and migrations stay applied.
sonnet.q4: In one load balancer change (step 10): the public listener is repointed from the old target group to the new one. There is no gradual shift.
sonnet.q5: A spike in the 5xx rate: above 1% over any 5-minute window within the 15 minutes after the switch. Rollback repoints the public listener to the old target group, tags the old colour live and the new one failed, then shuts down the new colour's 4 instances. It does not touch migrations.
sonnet.q6: 30 minutes after the switch (the rollback window), via a manual rollback job (step 13) while the old colour is up. After the old colour is shut down, the manual job is refused and a rollback is a normal deploy of the previous release. Nothing watches or alerts between minute 15 and 30.
sonnet.q7: Migrations that already finished stay applied; the failed one's state beyond that is not detailed, except an invalid index may be left by a failed concurrent build. The deploy stops, the new release never starts, and the live colour keeps serving. To recover, fix the cause, drop any invalid index and re-run the deploy.
sonnet.q8: Step 3 reads the target group the public listener forwards to. That group is live and the other is idle (receives the new release). The listener is the only record of the live colour.
sonnet.q9: The deploy lock, CI's concurrency group for catalog-web. It is held from step 1 until step 15, which can be up to 30 minutes after the switch. A second deploy queues and waits. (A manual rollback does not take the lock.)
sonnet.q10: Through the test listener, a second load balancer port reachable only from CI. Step 6 points its rule at the idle target group, while the public listener still forwards to the live colour.
sonnet.q11: Step 5 of the CI deploy run applies them with the migration tool, once, after lint and before any new instance starts. Its history table records what has run, and every migration uses IF NOT EXISTS, so a re-run is safe. Whether the tool itself prevents double runs is not otherwise stated.
sonnet.q12: They are shut down. In an abort, step 9 shuts down the new instances and leaves the idle colour empty. In an automatic rollback, step 12 shuts down the new colour and tags it failed. If a shutdown fails, step 2 of the next deploy shuts down the leftover instances. The next deploy repoints the test listener at the idle group.
